title: client-prewarm-and-tool-delegation-prd-exploration
content:
Purpose:

This is an exploratory PRD for two related Hosted API features intended to reduce perceived latency and improve developer ergonomics for long-running or tool-heavy flows: 1) client prewarm / session warm-up primitives that proactively prepare model runtime, KV caches, and tool bindings; 2) a lightweight tool delegation surface that lets clients build composable tool-call patterns and commit semantics for offline/async toollets.

Why we care (motivation):
- Customers building chat/agent clients report initial token latency spikes and repeated cold starts when switching models or routes.
- Tool-heavy flows (search + DB + code-exec wrappers) pay extra handshake and auth costs per invocation.
- SDK ergonomics for streaming currently force implementers to choose either purely optimistic streaming callbacks or heavyweight transactional semantics — we need a middle ground.
- Reducing tail-latency and smoothing the UX will directly improve PLG conversion and reduce support load for real-time apps.

High-level goals (success metrics):
- Reduce median time-to-first-byte for a new session by >= 40% for common web/chat workloads (metrics measured by Console telemetry).
- Reduce frequency of model-route cold starts in the first 60s of a session by 60%.
- Provide an SDK surface for delegable tools that reduces client-side glue code by 30% (qualitative: developer interviews).
- No regression in cost per token > 5% at platform level (prefetch must be throttleable/policy-able).

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Prewarm/session primitives exposed via Hosted API and SDKs (JS/TS and Python initial).
- Tool Delegation API: tokenized, idempotent tool handles with commit/abort semantics for offline results.
- Streaming interaction patterns that combine prewarm and tool delegation for progressive fidelity (low/medium/high).
- Telemetry, billing considerations, and rollout gating.

Out of scope:
- Full enterprise private deployment packaging (Private/Dedicated specific infra work will be tracked separately).
- New model compilation kernels — runtime team will provide prewarm hooks; this PRD is API/UX focused.

Design principles and constraints:
- Backwards-compatible: existing streaming and tool-call surfaces must continue to work with no changes for current customers.
- Opt-in: prewarm must never be automatically billed without consent; default idle-timeouts enforced.
- Observable: prewarm and delegated tool outcomes should emit traceable events and be surfaced in Console.
- Security-first: tool delegation tokens must support per-tool scopes, expiry, and optional re-auth via KMS.

User personas and primary flows:
1) Embedded chat widget (low-latency UX): prewarm session on page load to warm small KV cache for the last N messages and pre-resolve tool stubs for autocomplete and search.
2) Developer building a multi-tool agent: uses tool-delegate handles to register tool behaviors and compose them locally; server can commit tool outputs back to a hosted queue when available.
3) Mobile client with intermittent connectivity: prewarm reduces expensive cold handshake; tool-delegation supports offline queueing and later commit once connectivity returns.

Product surface (API + SDK sketches):
- HTTP API additions (minimal): POST /v1/sessions/prewarm 
  - body: {"session_id": "s-123", "model": "rw-gtl-7b", "tools": ["search:v2","db-query"], "kv_prefill": ["recent_messages"], "fidelity": "low|medium|high", "ttl_secs": 120}
  - response: 202 Accepted + {"prewarm_id":"pw-...","estimated_ready": 140ms}
  - semantics: returns immediately, attempts to allocate runtime artifacts, returns best-effort readiness.

- Streaming client SDK primitive (JS sketch):
  - sessions.prewarm({model, tools, ttl, fidelity}) -> Promise<PrewarmHandle>
  - prewarmHandle.on('ready', () => socket.open(...))
  - sessions.open({session_id, model, use_prewarm:true}) -> uses available prewarm to lower TTFB.

- Tool Delegation surface (idempotent handles):
  - sessions.delegateTool({name: 'search', scope: ['read'], offline: true}) -> ToolHandle
  - toolHandle.invoke({input, idempotencyKey}) -> returns immediate Ack + local placeholder stream
  - toolHandle.commit({idempotencyKey, resultBlob}) -> attempts to attach result server-side (optionally signed)
  - toolHandle.abort({idempotencyKey, reason})

Tool delegation semantics (notes):
- Invocation returns synchronously with a placement token (local placeholder) so streaming can continue.
- Commit attaches the actual results to the session and can trigger re-generation or patch streaming frames.
- SDKs expose small helper for optimistic local results (local caching of tool outputs with tombstones).

Streaming & progressive fidelity model:
- Fidelity hints: low (minimal context, fast, smaller model variant), medium (full context KV caching), high (full context + heavy tool verification).
- Prewarm requests should accept fidelity hint; runtime chooses kernel/model variant and may prepopulate KV caches accordingly.
- Progressive frames: streaming frames may carry a fidelity_tag: e.g., {frame_type: 'partial', fidelity: 'low', source: 'model'} or {frame_type: 'tool_patch', fidelity: 'high', tool: 'search'}
- Clients can subscribe to fidelity-tiered callbacks: onPartialLow, onPartialMedium, onPatchFromTool.

SDK ergonomics and examples (JS focused):
- Goal: minimize glue code to support optimistic streaming + tool commits.
- Minimal example: 
  const session = await client.sessions.open({session_id, model});
  const pw = await client.sessions.prewarm({model, tools:['search'], fidelity:'low', ttl:60});
  pw.on('ready', () => session.startStream());
  const search = client.sessions.delegateTool({name:'search', offline:true});
  search.invoke({q:'recent tickets', idempotencyKey:'abc'}) // returns placeholder
  // UI shows optimistic result while offline -> later commit

- SDK should provide small utilities: optimisticToolResult(storeKey, placeholder, ttl), reconcilePatch(patch), onFidelity(fn).

Telemetry & observability:
- Emit events: prewarm.requested, prewarm.ready, prewarm.failed, tool.invoke, tool.commit, tool.abort, fidelity.upgrade, fidelity.downgrade.
- Console dashboard: prewarm success rate by model/region, prewarm cost delta per customer, tool-delegation commit latency histograms.
- Correlate prewarm handles to traces for request-level debugging.

Billing considerations and cost controls:
- Prewarm should be meterable as a small per-minute reserved capacity line item (configurable by customer). Default behavior: free low-frequency prewarm (first N seconds free), then metered.
- Offer policy knobs: max_prewarm_concurrency, auto-cancel idle prewarm, fidelity cost multipliers.
- Tool-delegation commit/batching: commits should not create extra per-token charges beyond normal tool execution — but storage of committed blobs may be charged.

Security and compliance:
- Tool handles are minted tokens scoped to session and tool; support short expiry and optional rebind to customer-managed KMS markers.
- Ensure audit logs include commit/abort operations and associated user IDs.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (internal experiment): integrate prewarm hooks in serving-runtime + add SDK-flag. Instrument sample apps. (2 sprints)
- Phase 1 (beta): enable for selected customers, Console telemetry + billing flag. (4–6 weeks)
- Phase 2 (GA): public SDK release, default UI integration in Quickstart, pricing docs.

Open questions / design tradeoffs:
1) Billing model: free tier prewarm vs strictly metered. What are thresholds? (product & finance decision)
2) TTL semantics: should prewarm TTL be restart-on-use or fixed from allocation? (runtime-dependent)
3) Tool commit verification: do we re-run parts of generation to validate committed results or trust client-supplied signed blobs? (security vs latency)
4) Cross-model prewarm reuse: can a prewarm for a larger model be used to accelerate a smaller variant? (runtime engineering)
5) Offline tool storage location and retention policy — platform-managed vs customer-managed.

Next steps / immediate action items:
- Sync with serving-runtime to define the minimal prewarm lifecycle API by 2025-01-20. (action: Miguel)
- Add JIRA epic JIRA-API-3421 and break into prewarm runtime hooks + SDK changes + Console telemetry tasks. (action: Aisha)
- Prototype JS SDK surface in playground repo; ship experimental flag to internal beta. (action: Samir)
- Draft billing experiment and estimate cost delta for 50% active prewarm in demo orgs. (action: Priya)

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- This is intentionally exploratory with many UX sketches. Looking for feedback on the fidelity model, prewarm cost controls, and tool commit semantics.
- Please add concrete examples of mobile intermittent-network scenarios if you have telemetry / field reports.

Choppy brainstorm fragments (raw):
- prewarm 'hydration' vs 'reservation' distinction? hydration = populate caches on demand, reservation = keep runtime pinned
- should SDK expose 'prefetchProfile' templates (chat-widget, search-bot, ide-plugin)
- tool-delegation local placeholders could be JSON-LD blobs with stable ids
- try to reuse existing streaming frame types, add 'fidelity' enum rather than new framing protocol
